content.value: Prove that the lines $\begin{array} { r } { \frac { x - \alpha + d } { \alpha - \delta } = \frac { y - \alpha } { \alpha } = \frac { z - \alpha - d } { \alpha + \delta } } \end{array}$ and ${ \frac { x - b + c } { \beta - \gamma } } = { \frac { y - b } { \beta } } = { \frac { z - b - c } { \beta + \gamma } }$ are coplanar and find the equation of the plane in which they lie.
